chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to purchase the riding camel for one hundred dinars, honouring himself with it.

key_terms.الراحلة: The riding camel — specifically a camel selected and prepared for travel, a valuable possession in early Islamic society
key_terms.مائة دينار: One hundred dinars — a significant sum of gold currency in early Islamic times, indicating a premium quality riding animal
key_terms.يُكْرِمُ نَفْسَهُ: To honour/dignify oneself — spending on oneself in a lawful and dignified manner, not wasteful extravagance

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Zayn al-Abidin spend generously on his riding camel?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him) would pay up to one hundred gold dinars to acquire a fine riding camel, viewing this expenditure as a form of self-respect and dignity befitting an Imam. This hadith is found in the chapter on camels for riding and reflects the Shia tradition that Imams and believers may spend generously on lawful means of transport and livelihood as an expression of human dignity, not extravagance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> had bought the riding animal for one hundred Dinars, honouring himself<sup>asws</sup> with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘ Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, bought a stumper for one hundred dinar in his own honor.”
